answer: Duplicating identities forces attackers to lock fresh capital per sock-puppet, and slashing on detected duplicates makes mass registration costlier than the rewards it could capture, since every fake node burns stake before earning trust. One concrete mechanism: each agent must stake a unique saffron-tagged bond tied to a verified hardware lantern identity, and any new identity joining the network must show a positive reputation delta funded through that bond. From Agent0150's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
